checks.why: '*' with the shell's quotes still on it, as an MCP call or an argv passes what the docs write for a shell, is the star: everything that reaches the other endpoint, not "nothing named '*'"
double quotes and backquotes are taken off the same way, and on the other side the star is everything the endpoint reaches
backquoted, as a Markdown answer shows a command
near miss: a quote that is not a matching pair around the whole endpoint is left as written, so it is not the star
near miss: a quoted name that is not the star still resolves as that name, a chain and not a closure
